description: Kernel-line axis for the 0.11 release: eu.exeris:0.10.2 vs eu.exeris:0.11.0 vs eu.exeris.preview:0.11.0. The three coordinates cannot share a JDK, so the axis is run as a ladder in which every leg moves exactly one variable.
why_a_ladder: Class-file version plus the preview bit pin each kernel coordinate to a JDK: 0.10.2 is major 70 with 9/285 preview classes (JDK 26 only), mainline 0.11.0 is major 69 with no preview classes (JDK 25 through 28), preview/0.11.0 is major 72 with 95/306 preview classes (JDK 28 EA only).
A direct 0.10.2 vs preview/0.11.0 comparison therefore moves kernel version, JDK, and language/runtime feature set at once, and no part of the difference can be attributed.
Mainline 0.11.0 is the only coordinate that loads on more than one JDK, which makes it the bridge arm. Every leg below holds everything constant except the named variable.

The public SPI of mainline and preview 0.11.0 is identical apart from four records that become value class (TlsHandshakeResult, TlsShutdownResult, EventEngineStats, MemoryStats), so no application source differs across any arm.

arms.role: baseline: the kernel line currently pinned by every other community target
the release delta: identical app release, JDK and JVM flags as A, only the kernel version moves
bridge between the JDK-26 pair and the JDK ladder: same JDK as B, app dropped to release 25 and the preview flag removed
the shipping configuration: mainline 0.11.0 on the JDK 25 LTS, no preview anywhere
the JDK delta: byte-identical artifact to C, only the JVM feature release moves

the flag tax: byte-identical artifact to D on the same JDK, with only the preview flag toggled on. The flag is not free - it changes what the JVM will share from the default CDS archive - so this leg keeps that cost out of the Valhalla number

the recompile tax: same kernel as D-prime, but the app rebuilt at release 28 with preview. 30 of its 40 class files come out preview-marked from unchanged source (JEP 401 changes how the class-file format is read), so this cost belongs to the recompile, not to the preview kernel

the preview kernel at its FIRST cut: identical app build, JDK and flags as D-double-prime, only the kernel coordinate moves. Carries StructuredTaskScope plus six value classes - none of the six on a request path, which is why this arm alone cannot answer the Valhalla question. Arm F is the one that can.

the preview kernel with the carrier sweep: 159 JEP 401 value classes (157 value records plus RouteRequirement and CoreSslHandles) against E's six. Unlike E's six, these sit on the measured request path - HttpRequest, HttpResponse, HttpHeader, HttpStatus, RouteMatch, PathTemplate, Http1RequestParser, ReadResult, NativeTcpStreamPendingWrite, RequestPersistenceSession. There is no mainline 0.11.1: this version exists only under eu.exeris.preview.

legs.held_constant: app compiler release (26), JDK (26), preview flag (on)

legs.isolates: app compiler release 26 -> 25 and the preview flag going off
legs.claim: control - connects the JDK-26 pair to the JDK ladder; a large effect here means the ladder legs cannot be chained to the release delta
cost of staying on the LTS
flag tax, chiefly the default CDS archive

legs.isolates: app recompiled at release 28 with preview (30/40 class files become preview-marked)
kernel coordinate eu.exeris -> eu.exeris.preview (Valhalla value classes + StructuredTaskScope)
legs.claim: the Valhalla + structured-concurrency delta - the headline number for the preview line

legs.isolates: the JEP 401 carrier sweep: 6 -> 159 value classes, of which the new ones are on the request path
legs.held_constant: kernel groupId (eu.exeris.preview), JDK (28 EA), preview flag (on), app build (release 28 + preview)
legs.claim: the cleanest Valhalla leg this axis can produce - same coordinate, same toolchain, the value modifier is the variable. NOT a pure modifier delta: the same patch also carries the FileSink poison-pill fix and the CommunityRotatingKeySet CAS removal, both off the measured cleartext read path but both real code changes. Report the leg as 'preview 0.11.0 -> 0.11.1', never as 'value classes alone'.

legs.isolates: kernel coordinate eu.exeris:0.11.0 -> eu.exeris.preview:0.11.1 (StructuredTaskScope + the full carrier sweep)
legs.claim: distributed line vs the full preview line - the headline figure for adopting the preview coordinate. Measured directly rather than summed from D-double-prime->E and E->F, so it does not inherit either leg's error.

known_confounds: JDK 28 is an early-access build (28-ea+10-569) and JDK 25/26 are GA. EA builds may carry diagnostics and JIT tuning that GA does not, so every leg crossing into JDK 28 inherits an EA-vs-GA difference that no arm here can separate out.
Arm A is the only one whose staged jar shades a kernel with preview class files at major 70; it cannot be moved to any other JDK, so the release delta is only ever measurable at JDK 26.

Community persistence is JDBC over HikariCP, so on a DB-bound contract most of the response time is Postgres and kernel-internal effects compress. Read the light contract and the agent-free scenarios before the aggregate read.

The E->F patch is not modifier-only. Alongside the 159 value-class declarations it carries a FileSink shutdown fix (the poison pill was compared by identity, which value semantics breaks) and removes a compareAndSet on a record in CommunityRotatingKeySet. Both are off the measured cleartext read path - telemetry is disabled in the run env and key rotation is not on the entity-read path - but neither is nothing, so E->F is 'preview 0.11.0 -> 0.11.1', not 'the value modifier'.
